messages:
Alex Chen: Quick question — thinking about switching from our PPO to the HDHP during open enrollment so I can start contributing to an HSA. A few quick things I couldn't find in the guide: 1) Can I keep my existing HSA account with my current custodian if the new plan's carrier has a different recommended bank? 2) How does the employer match work if I switch mid-year — prorated? 3) I currently have a general-purpose FSA; do I need to change that to be eligible for HSA? Thanks!

Sara Patel: Hey @Alex — good Qs, nice and specific. Short answers up front: 1) Usually yes, you can keep your existing HSA custodian. 2) Employer match is prorated to the effective date. 3) You cannot have a general-purpose FSA and an HSA at the same time. Details below. :point_down:

Sara Patel: - HSA custodian: we don't mandate a specific bank for employee HSAs. If you keep your current HSA, you can continue contributions via payroll as long as the account accepts employer contributions. If the custodian needs a specific employer ID, we'll provide it — just CC benefits@redwood.com.

Sara Patel: - Employer contribution timing: match is prorated based on the plan effective date you choose during open enrollment. Example: if your employer annual match = $1,200 and your HDHP becomes effective 7/1, you'll get $600 total across the remainder of the year (paid on payroll cadence). Payroll may split that across remaining pay periods.

Sara Patel: - FSA incompatibility: general-purpose FSA prevents HSA eligibility. Options: 1) elect a limited-purpose FSA (dental/vision only) if offered, or 2) run out/terminate your general-purpose FSA before HDHP effective date. If you have a midyear change, submit FSA change form and we can coordinate.

Jamal Rivera: Adding payroll notes from my side — scheduling/timing: 
- Payroll cutover: changes that go into Workday before the benefits effective cutoff (see portal notice) will be implemented the 1st of the month effective date you pick. If the change is entered after cutoffs or has a mid-pay-period effective date, employer contributions typically start on the next payroll.
- Proration: we prorate at the calendar-month level, not by exact days. So switching effective 7/1 yields half-year proration.
- Action for custodian: if your HSA custodian requires a 1099 or employer ID, ping us and Payroll will supply the employer tax ID details.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: Open enrollment closes in 6 days. Submit elections by 11:59pm PDT on 1923550000.

Alex Chen: Thanks! Two follow-ups: 1) If my current custodian charges transfer fees to move funds later, does Redwood cover that? 2) What's the exact process I should follow (step-by-step) to make the switch and avoid accidentally losing contributions?

Sara Patel: Short on fee coverage: we don't reimburse custodian transfer fees by default. If there's an unusual case, we can escalate, but plan for the fee to be on the employee.

Sara Patel: Step-by-step (recommended):
1) In the enrollment portal, choose the HDHP and opt into HSA contributions. Select your desired effective date (we recommend the 1st of the month).
2) If you want to keep your existing HSA: email benefits@redwood.com with the custodian name + your account number (optional), and we’ll confirm employer contribution setup. Suggested email subject: `HSA custodian confirmation — Alex Chen`.
3) If you want to consolidate funds later: contact your current HSA custodian for an account transfer form (this is external to Redwood).
4) If you currently have a general-purpose FSA: file the FSA change/termination form in the portal so it ends before the HDHP effective date.
5) Confirm via the benefits confirmation email you receive after enrollment. If anything looks off, reply ASAP so we can correct prior to payroll cutoff.

Jamal Rivera: Also: if payroll has to coordinate a mid-pay-period adjustment, give us at least one full pay cycle notice so we can avoid delayed contributions. If you prefer, we can mark the employer match as a separate off-cycle if needed, but that requires a ticket to Payroll.

Alex Chen: Great — super helpful. I'll submit the portal change today and email benefits@redwood.com with custodian details. Appreciate the clear steps. :thumbsup:

Sara Patel: Perfect — thanks Alex. Ping here if anything blocks you or if the custodian asks for anything unusual.

Payroll Team: Noted — we'll watch for the Workday update and the email to benefits@redwood.com.
